title: Much Is Given, Much Is Required
body:
IUIC in the ClassRoom · 2026-03-21

Opens [Luke 12](/bible/luke/12) · [2 Esdras 1](/bible/2-esdras/1) · [Prov 8](/bible/proverbs/8) · [Deut 7](/bible/deuteronomy/7) · [1 Cor 14](/bible/1-corinthians/14) · [Gen 1](/bible/genesis/1) · [Wis 7](/bible/wisdom-of-solomon/7) · [Matt 9](/bible/matthew/9) · [2 Cor 5](/bible/2-corinthians/5) · [2 Cor 6](/bible/2-corinthians/6) · [Sir 44](/bible/sirach/44) · [Sir 45](/bible/sirach/45) · [Sir 46](/bible/sirach/46) · [Sir 47](/bible/sirach/47) · [Sir 48](/bible/sirach/48) · [Sir 49](/bible/sirach/49) · and 3 more below
## Introduction *[[12:38](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1qC2mwBgisM&t=758s)]* A leadership class at the Austin school on Luke 12:48. To whom much is given, much is required. The teacher walks the captains and officers through what the will of God is, why hypocrisy and covetousness are the two leavens Christ warned the disciples about as the multitudes came, and why the men who teach the people stand to a higher judgment than the people they teach. The class then traces where the wisdom that makes a man new comes from, Wisdom of Solomon 7, and reads through the famous men of Sirach 44 through 50 to show how a name is earned: by moving uprightly in the conversion of the people, standing firm when the people turn back, and repenting like David when you fall. ## Scriptures Opened **[Luke 12:47-48](/bible/luke/12#v47)** *[[15:37](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1qC2mwBgisM&t=937s)]* > [47](/bible/luke/12#v47) And that servant, which knew his lord’s will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes. > > [48](/bible/luke/12#v48) But he that knew not, and did commit things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes. For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: and to whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more. - The servant who knew his Lord's will and did not prepare himself is beaten with many stripes. The will of God is his law, so this is the man who knows the commandments and does not measure himself against them. - Preparing yourself means opening the book, reading it for what it says, and doing it. If Christ came back right now, many of us are not ready. - He that knew not is beaten with few stripes. The teacher gives a real example of two fornication cases judged differently: a sister in the truth only a few months who slipped with the husband she had for ten years was kept and corrected, while a brother who dealt with a sister was put out. Judgments are not always the same because the expectation is not the same. - Much was given to us. We were handed the keys to the kingdom, the will of God that people live a whole life without understanding. As you move up in rank the road gets narrower until you have to walk blameless. - To whom men have committed much, they will ask the more. If you have skills that can fill offices, more offices will be committed to you. If you cannot be used you are useless. Upper leadership keeps the phone on twenty-four hours a day because there is that much going on across Israel. Precepts: - **[Psalms 40:8](/bible/psalms/40#v8)** > [8](/bible/psalms/40#v8) I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart. I delight to do thy will; thy law is within my heart. God defines his will as his law, which is what the servant in Luke 12:47 knew and did not do. **[Luke 12:1-3](/bible/luke/12#v1)** *[[23:39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1qC2mwBgisM&t=1419s)]* > [1](/bible/luke/12#v1) In the mean time, when there were gathered together an innumerable multitude of people, insomuch that they trode one upon another, he began to say unto his disciples first of all, Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy. > > [2](/bible/luke/12#v2) For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; neither hid, that shall not be known. > > [3](/bible/luke/12#v3) Therefore whatsoever ye have spoken in darkness shall be heard in the light; and that which ye have spoken in the ear in closets shall be proclaimed upon the housetops. - An innumerable multitude gathered, treading on one another to get to the word. The first thing Christ told the disciples in that moment was to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy. - The people coming in are hungry for the word, so be careful how you move. A teacher who reads these scriptures while plotting on one of the sisters, robbing, or selling drugs will run the people off and change how the whole ministry is viewed. - Nothing covered shall not be revealed. Whatever you speak in darkness will be heard in the light and proclaimed on the housetops. You will not get away with it in this life or the one to come. **[Luke 12:15](/bible/luke/12#v15)** *[[27:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1qC2mwBgisM&t=1665s)]* > [15](/bible/luke/12#v15) And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth. - The second warning as the people come is covetousness. When the people come, the money comes with them. They buy into the system because they trust that these men are the mouthpiece of God. - A man's life does not consist in the abundance of the things he possesses. What you have does not make you who you are. - A captain adds that the people have had enough of pastors taking their tithes and flying jets. When they come here and see men professing to be men of God, they must see the change. The teacher agrees: we build schools all over the world and every man here holds a job. That is not the machine we are running. **[Luke 12:23-24](/bible/luke/12#v23)** *[[29:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1qC2mwBgisM&t=1757s)]* > [23](/bible/luke/12#v23) The life is more than meat, and the body is more than raiment. > > [24](/bible/luke/12#v24) Consider the ravens: for they neither sow nor reap; which neither have storehouse nor barn; and God feedeth them: how much more are ye better than the fowls? - Life is more than meat and the body more than raiment. Consider the ravens, which neither sow nor reap, yet God feeds them. - Christ kept pressing the same point to the twelve because he knew what was about to come in. Do not get distracted chasing riches, because it will lead you away from him. **[Luke 12:31-34](/bible/luke/12#v31)** *[[31:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1qC2mwBgisM&t=1917s)]* > [31](/bible/luke/12#v31) But rather seek ye the kingdom of God; and all these things shall be added unto you. > > [32](/bible/luke/12#v32) Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom. > > [33](/bible/luke/12#v33) Sell that ye have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth. > > [34](/bible/luke/12#v34) For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also. - Seek ye the kingdom of God and all these things shall be added. Seek doing the work and leading the people, and the Lord provides. Covetousness almost ripped this congregation apart in the past, along with deceit, hypocrisy, lying, and murmuring. - The teacher notes this class was almost titled Murmuring Is Witchcraft, because murmuring is done to alter the way you think about a person. That class is coming. - Fear not, little flock, for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom. He wants us to have it. There is no greater gift than to know the word of God and have the opportunity to teach it. - Sell that ye have and give alms does not mean make yourself homeless. It means do not hoard three or four cars and five or six homes while the ministry lacks, because where your treasure is, there your heart will be also. - If God wants to give us the kingdom and not them, then we are special to him. He gives wisdom and requires something back, which is fair. **[2 Esdras 1:17-25](/bible/2-esdras/1#v17)** *[[37:18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1qC2mwBgisM&t=2238s)]* > [17](/bible/2-esdras/1#v17) Where are the benefits that I have done for you? when ye were hungry and thirsty in the wilderness, did ye not cry unto me, > > [18](/bible/2-esdras/1#v18) Saying, Why hast thou brought us into this wilderness to kill us? it had been better for us to have served the Egyptians, than to die in this wilderness. > > [19](/bible/2-esdras/1#v19) Then had I pity upon your mournings, and gave you manna to eat; so ye did eat angels’ bread. > > [20](/bible/2-esdras/1#v20) When ye were thirsty, did I not cleave the rock, and waters flowed out to your fill? for the heat I covered you with the leaves of the trees. > > [21](/bible/2-esdras/1#v21) I divided among you a fruitful land, I cast out the Canaanites, the Pherezites, and the Philistines, before you: what shall I yet do more for you? saith the Lord. > > [22](/bible/2-esdras/1#v22) Thus saith the Almighty Lord, When ye were in the wilderness, in the river of the Amorites, being athirst, and blaspheming my name, > > [23](/bible/2-esdras/1#v23) I gave you not fire for your blasphemies, but cast a tree in the water, and made the river sweet. > > [24](/bible/2-esdras/1#v24) What shall I do unto thee, O Jacob? thou, Juda, wouldest not obey me: I will turn me to other nations, and unto those will I give my name, that they may keep my statutes. > > [25](/bible/2-esdras/1#v25) Seeing ye have forsaken me, I will forsake you also; when ye desire me to be gracious unto you, I shall have no mercy upon you. - Where are the benefits that I have done for you? When you cried in the wilderness he had pity and gave you manna, angels' bread. He cleaved the rock, covered you with leaves, divided a fruitful land, and cast out the Canaanites and Philistines before you. What shall I yet do more for you? - When you blasphemed at the river of the Amorites he did not give fire for it but made the water sweet. He fed you because you are special to him. - What shall I do unto thee, O Jacob? Thou Judah wouldst not obey me. Seeing you have forsaken me, I will forsake you. He charged you to be over his people and lead them to him, and you take their money and walk in hypocrisy. Many stripes. - The teacher plays a clip of another camp's street preacher to make the point that those men are not the example, though they are still our brothers and we pray for their repentance. We want a different program here, and when we are in error we correct it among ourselves. **[Proverbs 8:12-19](/bible/proverbs/8#v12)** *[[42:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1qC2mwBgisM&t=2540s)]* > [12](/bible/proverbs/8#v12) I wisdom dwell with prudence, and find out knowledge of witty inventions. > > [13](/bible/proverbs/8#v13) The fear of the Lord is to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth, do I hate. > > [14](/bible/proverbs/8#v14) Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom: I am understanding; I have strength. > > [15](/bible/proverbs/8#v15) By me kings reign, and princes decree justice. > > [16](/bible/proverbs/8#v16) By me princes rule, and nobles, even all the judges of the earth. > > [17](/bible/proverbs/8#v17) I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me. > > [18](/bible/proverbs/8#v18) Riches and honour are with me; yea, durable riches and righteousness. > > [19](/bible/proverbs/8#v19) My fruit is better than gold, yea, than fine gold; and my revenue than choice silver. - Wisdom dwells with prudence. The fear of the Lord is to hate evil, pride, arrogancy, the evil way, and the froward mouth. By wisdom kings reign and princes decree justice. Leaders reign by wisdom. - The success of Israel United in Christ is that we are sincere about keeping the commandments and enforcing them among the children of Israel, on top of believing on the black Messiah. That is what brings the masses in. Not the camps that smoke weed or keep multiple wives they do not take care of. - I love them that love me. God chose us first, and now he says love me back. Be what I called you to be. He is making you special and you are making yourself unspecial. - Those that seek me early shall find me. People start looking for God in prison or when the disease comes. You cannot walk in hypocrisy your whole life, then cry to him in a dilemma and expect favor. - Riches and honor are with me, durable riches and righteousness. My fruit is better than gold. The riches we want are not money but the word dwelling in us richly. Precepts: - **[Colossians 3:16](/bible/colossians/3#v16)** > [16](/bible/colossians/3#v16) Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord. Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom, teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs. Those are the durable riches Proverbs 8 speaks of. **[Deuteronomy 7:6-10](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v6)** *[[48:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1qC2mwBgisM&t=2882s)]* > [6](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v6) For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth. > > [7](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v7) The Lord did not set his love upon you, nor choose you, because ye were more in number than any people; for ye were the fewest of all people: > > [8](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v8) But because the Lord loved you, and because he would keep the oath which he had sworn unto your fathers, hath the Lord brought you out with a mighty hand, and redeemed you out of the house of bondmen, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt. > > [9](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v9) Know therefore that the Lord thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations; > > [10](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v10) And repayeth them that hate him to their face, to destroy them: he will not be slack to him that hateth him, he will repay him to his face. - Thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, chosen to be a special people above all people on the face of the earth. What makes us holy is the law, because the law is holy and the commandment holy, just, and good. - The word of God has no power unless you activate it, and the only way to activate it is to do what it says. Otherwise it is words on a page. You become the living example of what a holy people is. - The nations already witness it at the big events: thousands of men mobilized on the street with nobody smoking, nobody fighting, and the place clean when they file back in. That is the word working through us. Compare that to how the world laughed at the crowds at the rodeo in Houston. - He did not choose us because we were more in number. We were the fewest, and he chose us because he loved us. Thank you, Lord, for choosing this lot. - He keeps covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments, and repays them that hate him to their face. If you use a leadership position to beguile sisters into sex, to keep them in a filthy mindset, or to take advantage of people for money, God will judge you. You hate God and you hate his people. - Let the sisters get counsel from sisters. When you do give counsel, it must be what God wants them to hear and beneficial to them, not to your own wants. Precepts: - **[Leviticus 20:26](/bible/leviticus/20#v26)** > [26](/bible/leviticus/20#v26) And ye shall be holy unto me: for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine. Ye shall be holy unto me, for I the Lord am holy and have severed you from other people. Offered from the floor as the scripture behind being a holy people. - **[Romans 7:12](/bible/romans/7#v12)** > [12](/bible/romans/7#v12) Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good. The law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good. The law is what makes Israel a holy people. - **[Matthew 9:36](/bible/matthew/9#v36)** > [36](/bible/matthew/9#v36) But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd. A captain's precept. Christ was moved with compassion because the multitudes fainted and were scattered as sheep having no shepherd. That is what motivates leaders to deny themselves the riches and the women and rebuild the nation. - **[Sirach 37:19](/bible/sirach/37#v19)** > [19](/bible/sirach/37#v19) There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself. A captain's precept. There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself. Leaders in the other camps know the laws but their god is money or power over the people, so they are unprofitable to themselves, and nothing will stay hid. **[1 Corinthians 14:33-35](/bible/1-corinthians/14#v33)** *[[1:02:32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1qC2mwBgisM&t=3752s)]* > [33](/bible/1-corinthians/14#v33) For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints. > > [34](/bible/1-corinthians/14#v34) Let your women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but they are commanded to be under obedience, as also saith the law. > > [35](/bible/1-corinthians/14#v35) And if they will learn any thing, let them ask their husbands at home: for it is a shame for women to speak in the church. - God is not the author of confusion but of peace. If a woman will learn anything, let her ask her husband at home. - Her husband is the one she goes to for wisdom and understanding, not another man. If she goes to another man it causes confusion, and no husband wants to hear that a bishop, deacon, or captain said otherwise. - Some men who are leaders will come in and beguile your wife. It is not for any brother here to instruct another man's wife in the scriptures or to investigate what another man's wife or daughters know. That is not your business. - A captain adds that sisters from other camps say the leaders there immediately try to get their number, and here we roll different. We have processes in place because everyone coming in is still battling their own lust. A man will cleave to his like, so examine which example you are cleaving to. **[Genesis 1:26-28](/bible/genesis/1#v26)** *[[1:05:14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1qC2mwBgisM&t=3914s)]* > [26](/bible/genesis/1#v26) And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth. > > [27](/bible/genesis/1#v27) So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. > > [28](/bible/genesis/1#v28) And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth. - Let us make man in our image, after our likeness, and let them have dominion. God's image is the greatest image there is, and he mirrored man after himself. That is why we are special. - God blessed them with his image and with dominion, but the blessing did not end there. Precepts: - **[Genesis 2:7](/bible/genesis/2#v7)** > [7](/bible/genesis/2#v7) And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul. The Lord God breathed into his nostrils the breath of life and man became a living soul. The breath of life is wisdom; it is what activated us and set us apart from every other nation. **[Wisdom of Solomon 7:22-27](/bible/wisdom-of-solomon/7#v22)** *[[1:10:54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1qC2mwBgisM&t=4254s)]* > [22](/bible/wisdom-of-solomon/7#v22) For wisdom, which is the worker of all things, taught me: for in her is an understanding spirit holy, one only, manifold, subtil, lively, clear, undefiled, plain, not subject to hurt, loving the thing that is good quick, which cannot be letted, ready to do good, > > [23](/bible/wisdom-of-solomon/7#v23) Kind to man, steadfast, sure, free from care, having all power, overseeing all things, and going through all understanding, pure, and most subtil, spirits. > > [24](/bible/wisdom-of-solomon/7#v24) For wisdom is more moving than any motion: she passeth and goeth through all things by reason of her pureness. > > [25](/bible/wisdom-of-solomon/7#v25) For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her. > > [26](/bible/wisdom-of-solomon/7#v26) For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God, and the image of his goodness. > > [27](/bible/wisdom-of-solomon/7#v27) And being but one, she can do all things: and remaining in herself, she maketh all things new: and in all ages entering into holy souls, she maketh them friends of God, and prophets. - Wisdom, the worker of all things, taught me. In her is an understanding spirit. That is why we understand the Bible and why people ask how we have a scripture for everything. - She is holy, lively, clear, undefiled, plain, loving the thing that is good, kind to man, steadfast, sure, and free from care. Free from the cares of this world. - Wisdom has all power and oversees all things. Tether yourself to wisdom and everything becomes plain: there is no way to be close to God while sinning unchecked and expect the kingdom. - A sister came into the truth because she saw the camp in the street and was amazed that none of the brothers tried to talk to her. That is the example working. Do not be the slick one that ruins it. - She is the breath of the power of God and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty; no defiled thing can fall into her. If wisdom flows from God and is influencing you, you are tethered to God. Anything else influencing you is covetousness or lust. - She is the unspotted mirror of the power of God and the image of his goodness. Remaining in herself, she maketh all things new. Wisdom makes you new, so you cannot keep doing the same things. - In all ages she enters holy souls and makes them friends of God and prophets. She cannot dwell in a body subject to sin, hypocrisy, covetousness, or hatred. When you move like that you start saying absurd things. A prophet's job is to raise up God's children, which is why he cannot walk in hypocrisy. Precepts: - **[Mark 4:18-19](/bible/mark/4#v18)** > [18](/bible/mark/4#v18) And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, > > [19](/bible/mark/4#v19) And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful. Sown among thorns: the cares of this world, the deceitfulness of riches, and the lust of other things choke the word. Wisdom is free from those cares, so a man with wisdom does not entertain covetousness. - **[Hebrews 4:10-12](/bible/hebrews/4#v10)** > [10](/bible/hebrews/4#v10) For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his. > > [11](/bible/hebrews/4#v11) Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief. > > [12](/bible/hebrews/4#v12) For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart. Labor to enter into that rest. The word of God is quick and powerful and a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart. The power of God is his word, which is wisdom, and it governs the intents where sin begins. - **[Psalms 19:7-8](/bible/psalms/19#v7)** > [7](/bible/psalms/19#v7) The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple. > > [8](/bible/psalms/19#v8) The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes. The law converts the soul, the testimony makes wise the simple, the commandment is pure and enlightens the eyes. The pure influence of Wisdom of Solomon 7:25 is the statutes of God, and once converted we are new. - **[1 Samuel 10:6](/bible/1-samuel/10#v6)** > [6](/bible/1-samuel/10#v6) And the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man. The spirit of the Lord comes upon thee and thou shalt be turned into another man. If the word is dealing with you but you still live the old man, the Lord says many stripes. - **[Luke 6:45-49](/bible/luke/6#v45)** > [45](/bible/luke/6#v45) A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is evil: for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh. > > [46](/bible/luke/6#v46) And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say? > > [47](/bible/luke/6#v47) Whosoever cometh to me, and heareth my sayings, and doeth them, I will shew you to whom he is like: > > [48](/bible/luke/6#v48) He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock. > > [49](/bible/luke/6#v49) But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great. Why call ye me Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say? The man who hears and does is built on the rock and endures when the flood beats on the house. Brothers asking about deep prophecy while still on pornography need to learn themselves first. - **[James 1:27](/bible/james/1#v27)** > [27](/bible/james/1#v27) Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world. Pure religion undefiled is to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction and to keep himself unspotted from the world. No brother should be instructing or examining another man's wife or daughters. - **Why could David still be counted among the famous men after his sin?** He repented.
